notes.title: What do Welfare State, Robber Baron, Epidemic and Bohemian Life have in common?
notes.content: [p]Let's dive a little bit into another aspect of the game: [i]Scenarios[/i], which you can choose at the beginning of the game.[/p][p][i]Scenarios[/i] determine the starting conditions and progression of a run: from the general characteristics of the map, to the resources available, from the initial buildings, to the modifiers applied throughout the game.[/p][p]These are the 19th century inspired [i]Scenarios[/i] that are currently planned for the full game:[/p][list][*][p][u]First Steps[/u] (the tutorial): normal starting conditions, learn the basics of the game.[/p][/*][*][p][u]The Love of Science[/u]: build a highly educated city, focusing on [i]Research[/i] and technology.[/p][/*][*][p][u]Welfare State[/u]: implement workers reforms and rights to your citizens, with a focus on signing new [i]Laws[/i].[/p][/*][*][p][u]Robber Baron[/u]: make your city function with low taxes, no workers rights, no welfare.[/p][/*][*][p][u]Epidemic[/u]: an epidemic in your city will require that you manage waves of infections, quarantines and vaccine distribution.[/p][/*][*][p][u]Bohemian Life[/u]: build a city based on entertainment: by and for the artists.[/p][/*][/list][p]I plan on adding more of them before the full game is released.[/p][p]Once you choose a [i]Scenario[/i] and start building your city, you will be faced with different choices of [i]Goals[/i] and [i]Rewards[/i], linked with the topic that is being tackled, as well as scheduled [i]Situations[/i], which are significant changes in your city that will require you to first plan ahead and then react once they happen.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/9edc7df684626a66046bed3980e25f8deef34098.jpg"][/img][/p][p]I'm going to run a closed beta when it's ready.  [/p][p]You can join by subscribing to the newsletter: [url="https://subscribepage.io/pressingthumbs/"]https://subscribepage.io/pressingthumbs/[/url][/p][p]Once the beta is ready, you will be notified there and receive a key for testing.[/p]

notes.title: Simulating the economy in Times of Progress
notes.content:
Lately  I have been working on implementing the core of the economy simulation in the game.

At a high level, this is how it works:
[list]
[*] Industries receive payments when they deliver the materials they extract or goods they produce.
[*] Their workers get paid a [i]Wage [/i]at the end of each month.
[*] [i]Citizens [/i]are organised in families. At the end of each month, those that work in each family (normally the adults, but, depending on your city [i]Laws[/i], it might be the children too, since we're in the 1800s), put together their earned wages and purchase the [i]Consumer Goods[/i] they need.
[*] These are organised by priority, first they'll buy [i]Food[/i], then better [i]Clothes[/i], then better [i]Furniture [/i]etc. Eventually if they earn more and have extra income, they'll spend their money in [i]Entertainment [/i](at the [i]Pub [/i]or [i]Theatre[/i]) and [i]Prestige [/i]items ([i]Fancy Clothes[/i], [i]Pottery[/i], etc.).
[*] Since there are also [i]Public Services[/i] in the city ([i]Police[/i], [i]School[/i], [i]Hospital [/i]etc), their workers will be civil servants. Meaning that they get paid by the [i]Taxes [/i]collected by the [i]City Hall[/i].
[/list]

All these systems connect with the rest of the mechanics in the game. For example:
[list]
[*] Eating enough and having better [i]Clothes [/i]improves [i]Health[/i].
[*] The level of [i]Education [/i]acquired by the [i]Citizens [/i]determines their [i]Wage[/i], which means they can afford more and better goods, while increasing productivity of their workplace. Although, while they study, they won't work and earn a wage.
[*] As more families have more of their needs met, from basic necessities to [i]Entertainment [/i]and [i]Prestige[/i], their houses will upgrade, which will increase the size of your city, with the perks and drawbacks that it brings.
[/list]

I have also added a few new buildings in the game:

The [i]Market[/i], where citizens buy their [i]Consumer Goods[/i]:
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/7eac85d0cfa584627d1999fadc578bf36c1fb68c.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/1be52e60d2db8a0af087696620ad2aa09d421eac.png[/img][/url]
The [i]City Hall[/i], where you will sign your chosen [i]Laws [/i]and manage the city.
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/be41980e7caabfbcea29b9fdecd9757f7aaa0ebd.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/f1ccee1c7de0ab8966b4bfe5d18fe2e6121ffc4c.png[/img][/url]
The [i]Research Institute[/i], where [i]Inventions [/i]can be unlocked.
[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/286c00c07dc971048c7bcca79e78c3da80947d32.png][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/2d5b2ac465eab293a0ce4b314dbb8252154c29af.png[/img][/url]
And more buildings that I will present in future announcements.

I have also finally implemented railways traveling in two directions, no more single rail, finally!

Vehicles will stop automatically to yield to other vehicles, based on priority and direction of travel. There won't be micromanagement of intersections and traffic, so you can focus on growing the city and making your citizens happy.

notes.title: A deep dive into the Progress Timeline UI
notes.content:
With this update I would like to show you the [i]Progress Timeline UI[/i], which is where you will be acquiring [i]Inventions[/i] and signing [i]Laws[/i] in [i]Times of Progress[/i].

The overall idea is that there will be new [i]Inventions[/i] and [i]Laws[/i] available following a timeline from 1800 to 1900, which is where the game takes place. These upgrades mirror real-life technological and legal advancement from the 19th century.

Here is how the UI looks:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/6622bc34804bdb5d240e4cb33326d74b56645b04.jpg[/img]

And here is an assortment of the kind of upgrades available (click to enlarge):

[table]
[tr]
[td][url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/6fa2aa4a0cc411913456a272703b20022cfb2559.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/2b369aa19dd626cd3e7b829952147a25e6eb9ba6.jpg[/img][/url][/td]
[td][url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/ef5e43a3cf57552c9eb4c43e8affdfd0e1804472.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/1a36727364b06ccbf76b0fe55efff0a992c182a0.jpg[/img][/url][/td]
[td][url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/aaf2a0ca86e2e1227769f20a2a9223385c647d61.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/8746c952f88942b756e3e5bc19e604b0a818e244.jpg[/img][/url][/td]
[/tr]
[tr]
[td][url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/4be72f75146e9b08cfea3eaa51102694553a45f9.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/604c32c94a744ee7037e8b74662eb177a89dccf8.jpg[/img][/url][/td]
[td][url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/8ccb15f9875985a14a1b6eb53c936502e5c090a1.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/beb2467c4f86779e06a6514b2ebc0cb46710b28c.jpg[/img][/url][/td]
[td][url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/537e051b32edbae67d13c64a65e31a84b3e742bb.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/12c06938e1fbbeb8c7835a481ed007da4c222248.jpg[/img][/url][/td]
[/tr]
[/table]

Some upgrades will be dependent on a previous upgrade being acquired or signed, and all upgrades will depend on having reached their year along the timeline.

However, you will be able to spend [i]Research[/i] and [i]Political Points[/i] to make these upgrades happen sooner. This represents your city's scientists and lawmakers contributing to the global community with their research so that these inventions and laws happen sooner, for the greater good!

This will mean that upgrade nodes in the [i]Progress Timeline UI[/i] will move upwards, so as a player you will also have agency over the upgrade tree and have more strategic choices to make when it comes to spending your hard earned [i]Research[/i] and [i]Political Points[/i]. Will you invest on making fewer upgrades happen sooner or will you wait and use the points to acquire more upgrades when they naturally become available?

Do you have any questions or feedback about this feature?

I would love to hear from you. Feel free to comment on this announcement, get in touch with the methods listed in the footer or send an email to: [i]support@pressingthumbs.com[/i]

notes.title: Times Of Progress is an elegant, focussed city builder set during the Industrial Revolution
notes.content:
Times Of Progress is a special game for me, because it's the first news tip I have ever received from Sin Vega, Prime Minister of Strategy Gaming. Sin once described writing news articles for our former news editor Alice0 (RPS in peace) as like practising backflips in front of the kung fu master. Writing about a new city builder at Sin's suggestion is like being invited to budget the development of Londinium by Julius Caesar.

The terror of screwing it up - together with other, more trivial distractions, like international games industry conferences - has stopped me from writing about Times Of Progress for months. Today I bite the bullet, and emerge from my lodgings to issue a hesitant speech to the masses, hoping like hell that Caesar is too preoccupied with the latest Gaul uprising to notice my errors.

notes.title: Set goals for your city, become an industrial powerhouse
notes.content:
Let's dive a bit deeper into one of the core ideas in [i]Times of Progress[/i]. As you know, the Industrial Revolution was a global phenomenon and in [i]ToP [/i]that is represented by the fact that your city does not exist in a void. 

As I discussed in a previous announcement (if you missed it you can read more about it [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2628450/view/5997186379223382084?l=english]here[/url]), new inventions are happening throughout the game world, not just in the local [i]Research Institute[/i] in your own city. 

You can import those new technologies by spending [i]Research Points[/i]. One of the ways in which you can earn them is by showing to the world that your city is at the forefront of industrial progress, in terms of quantity, quality and efficiency of your industries, products and transportation networks. You can do that by setting, and achieving, quantitative [i]Goals[/i] for your city and building a sort of reputation in the game world. 

This is how choosing new [i]Goals[/i] works:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/e5c42d41285f978ca792292f0beae92293855f8c.gif[/img]

You will be given some alternatives of what you would like to obtain, and for each [i]Goal[/i] there will be a [i]Reward[/i] associated with it, as well the corresponding amount of [i]Research Points[/i] that will be earned. 

[i]Goals[/i] can be reached, for example, by reaching a certain population, or transporting a specified amount of a resource, or upgrading a predefined number of houses to their next level.

On the other hand, examples of [i]Rewards[/i] can be an increase in efficiency of a specific building, or a reduction in the cost to build a new factory, or a type of vehicle traveling faster or transporting more.

[i]Rewards[/i] are usually incremental quantitative improvements to your buildings. They are designed so that individually they don't contribute a whole lot, but by choosing wisely which ones to pursue, their effects can definitely stack up and in turn make certain future [i]Goals[/i] easier to achieve. 

You can set more than one [i]Goal[/i] for yourself to work on at the same time and once you reach one, pick another. There are also upgrades that let you increase how many active [i]Goals[/i] you can have, as well as expand the choices available when setting them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/6124055047de6fe509a4d4868830a8beaff0728a.gif[/img]

notes.title: Signing laws to improve your citizens' lives
notes.content:
Let's dive a bit into the [i]Laws[/i] mechanic and the [i]City Hall[/i] building.

They are the administrative equivalent of [i]Research[/i] upgrades and the [i]Research Institute[/i] building. I talked about those in a previous newsletter issue. If you missed it, you can read up about it here: [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2628450/view/5997186379223382084?l=english]https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2628450/view/5997186379223382084?l=english[/url]

The [i]City Hall[/i] is a building that allows you to start signing [i]Laws [/i]for your citizens that unlock new buildings, change stats and affect the needs of the population.

Signing [i]Laws [/i]requires [i]Political Points[/i], which are obtained by completing [i]Goals [/i](like[i] Research Points[/i]) or passively via various buildings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/d99a0b5ad8f980b1cd8aa6a9a4803105b2ab6d14.jpg[/img]

Here are some examples of [i]Laws [/i]that you can decide to sign in [i]Times of Progress[/i], with their implications and the chain of laws that are made available:﻿
[list]
[*] [i]Public Health[/i] → [i]Disease Prevention[/i] and [i]Anatomy Act[/i].
[list]
[*] [i]Public Health[/i] increases the efficiency of [i]Infirmaries [/i]and makes available a few new possible laws. 
[*] [i]Disease Prevention[/i] unlocks laws that reduce [i]Health [/i]risks (having good [i]Health [/i]is one of the citizen's [i]Needs[/i]).
[*] [i]Anatomy Act[/i] (donating corpses to science) allows [i]Infirmaries[/i] and [i]Hospitals [/i]to passively produce[i] Research Points[/i].
[/list]
[*] [i]Citizen Assemblies[/i] → [i]Trade Unions[/i] → [i]Safety Regulations in Mines[/i].
[list]
[*] [i]Citizen Assemblies[/i] allow to produce [i]Political Points[/i] at [i]Pubs [/i](a building used for [i]Entertainment Need[/i]).
[*] [i]Trade Unions[/i] allow workers to unionize, giving a permanent efficiency boost, but making them more expensive. They also play a role with worker strikes, one of the possible events in the game.
[*] [i]Safety Regulations in Mines[/i] decrease efficiency in mines, but reduce the negative [i]Health [/i]effects for their workers. 
[/list]
[*] [i]Police Act[/i] → [i]Prison Reform[/i] → [i]Law & Order[/i].
[list]
[*] [i]Police Act[/i] unlocks the [i]Police Station[/i] building, needed to prevent crime and address the [i]Safety Need[/i].
[*] [i]Prison Reform[/i] increases the [i]Police Station[/i] number of workers needed and its efficiency. 
[*] [i]Law & Order[/i] allows [i]Police Stations[/i] to passively produce [i]Political Points[/i], but decreases [i]Safety [/i]and [i]Health [/i]of citizens in range.
[/list][/list]
Hope you find this mechanic interesting! As you see from the examples, it's very interconnected with other systems in the game, contributing to its sandbox nature.

notes.title: 19th century inventions and Times of Progress research tree
notes.content:
Let's talk about the [i]Research Tree[/i]. As you know, the game is set during the Industrial Revolution. It starts in 1800 and the research upgrades are planned throughout the century, mimicking real-world inventions that happened during the period.

However, it won't be the scientists in your city who all invent the [i]Steam Engine[/i], [i]Cement[/i], [i]Organic Chemistry[/i], the [i]Typewriter [/i]etc etc. That would be a handful of very formidable scientists!
Instead, your city is part of the Revolution happening throughout the (game) world and unlocking technologies in-game means importing them from outside of the city.

New inventions are scheduled along a timeline, but don't unlock until you spend points on them, like in any tech tree.
What your scientists at your local [i]Research Institute[/i] can do, instead, is accelerate the arrival of this new tech, meaning that you will actually be able to change the location of nodes in the research tree.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/6ad8c0560741babc2df0351dd4322f16f945c2ea.gif[/img]

Here are some chains of inventions and their effects:
[list]
[*] [i]Electrolysis [/i]→[i] Atomic Theory [/i]→ [i]Dynamite [/i]→ [i]Tunneling[/i].
For example, [i]Dynamite [/i]gives you the ability to remove small Hills and Mountains on the map that block your way, [i]Tunneling [/i]allows you to place [i]Railways [/i]inside Hills and Mountains directly.
[*] [i]Water Frame [/i]→ [i]Spinning Mule[/i] →[i] Sewing Machine[/i] → [i]Jeans[/i].
For example, [i]Sewing Machine[/i] improves efficiency in clothing industry buildings but reduces the number of workers needed, increasing unemployment. [i]Jeans [/i]improve miners efficiency and health.
[*] [i]Aluminum [/i]→ [i]Food Canning[/i] → [i]Hall-Héroult Process[/i].
Here [i]Aluminum [/i]unlocks the [i]Smelter [/i]and is a new tradable material. [i]Food Canning[/i] unlocks the [i]Cannery [/i]and the ability to store and distribute [i]Food [/i]more efficiently. [i]Hall-Héroult Process[/i] increases the production rate of smelters and the number of workers needed, so more employment is possible.
[/list]

Here is what makes it endlessly replayable: 
[list]
[*][i]Procedurally generated maps[/i]: this is self-explanatory: they will depend on some parameters that manage the amount of resources and terrain types available on the map.
[*][i]Randomised starting conditions to choose from[/i]: This means that apart from the amount of resources available on the map, you will also be able to choose some buildings you can start with, the resources available at the start in your storage, the resources that immigrants will bring with them etc.
[*][i]Randomised goals and rewards to choose from[/i]: A key part of the game loop is setting Goals for yourself to achieve (eg: transport 100 Coal by Train) and you will receive an associated Reward from it. It can be an increase in efficiency, or your industries will process goods a bit faster etc. These are the small increments that help you improve your city. There are other more sizeable upgrades, such as unlocking new buildings but that happens via a typical Research Tree.
[/list]

notes.title: So your workers are now on strike. What can you do about that?
notes.content:
With Labour Day having been celebrated a few days ago, I thought that this time I would go into some details about one of my favourite mechanics in the game: [i]Worker Strikes[/i].

Strikes are one of the Issues that can happen in [i]Times of Progress[/i], along with [i]Crime[/i], [i]Emigration[/i], [i]Prison Evasion[/i] and others.

To trigger them, a certain percentage of the [i]Workers [/i]in a specific place of work needs to not have received "payment" (in the form of [i]Food[/i]) for a few consecutive weeks. The thresholds are variable, based on upgrades and debuffs, but they are deterministic, there's no RNG involved. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/256272d52cd4de2736443b4b17a37e31bdc98d95.gif[/img]
Once the conditions are met, the [i]Strike [/i]starts, which means that [i]Production [/i]stops at the affected building and you get notified in the [i]Events [/i]panel.

What can you do about [i]Strikes[/i], you ask? Well, once they happen you can choose between:
[list]
[*] You can meet the demands of the [i]Workers [/i](get a one-off extra [i]Food [/i]portion, plus they'll consume slightly more going forward but they'll go back immediately to work).
[*] You can send the [i]Police [/i]to force them back to work (you save on the extra rations, but they'll get a productivity debuff).
[/list]
But there are also other mechanics that influence [i]Strikes[/i]:
[list]
[*] An upgrade allows you to choose to let them [i]Unionise [/i](per building type). This means that [i]Workers [/i]will have a permanent efficiency boost, but will consume more.
[*] [i]University [/i]educated workers are slightly more likely to go on [i]Strike [/i](but they have other benefits from being highly educated).
[*] Some [i]Workers [/i]never go on [i]Strike[/i], for example those in [i]Infirmaries [/i]and [i]Hospitals[/i], but instead their [i]Health [/i]decreases more quickly when they skip meals.
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/5bca3b4366ce4c435e8a2d90c7f20af14f09cac3.gif[/img]

As a development update: I am currently busy working on the UI and some game mechanics. To get to the closed beta I still need to wrap up what I am doing and move onto polishing, making the UI look good and adding sounds and soundtrack. Progress is steady, but there's a lot to do! I will keep you posted as always.

notes.title: A dynamic Orders System for maximum flexibility
notes.content:
I’ve been busy with the [i]Orders System[/i] lately, so I thought I would tell you a little about it.

In “[i]Times of Progress[/i]”, like any other resource management games, resources need to get from warehouses to industries and back.

There are no manually set routes though: an industry that needs a certain [i]Resource[/i] will look for the closest [i]Depot[/i] (or its larger version, a [i]Warehouse[/i]) and issue an [i]Order[/i] to it, requesting a certain amount of the [i]Resource[/i] they need (eg: [i]Coal[/i]).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/4b27b7945abebdb808e9440fb9df516da48ee4a6.gif[/img]

The [i]Depot[/i] then sends to the industry their [i]Coal[/i] and the industry starts producing.

[i]Depots[/i] also issue [i]Orders[/i] themselves: they are constantly trying to refill their stock from nearby industries.

The system is very flexible: if you decide to delete a [i]Depot[/i], industries will look for another one, which might be a little further away. The same goes for industries being deleted, or not being currently active: the [i]Depot[/i] will try to refill its stock from somewhere else, fully dynamically.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/d98c6cc8809527296c6d6b7108510b3279ef35e5.gif[/img]

The same goes when adding new [i]Depots[/i], or expanding the [i]Road[/i] or [i]Railway[/i] system: as soon as there’s a more efficient route to get the resources needed, it will be chosen automatically by the game, giving maximum flexibility and avoiding any tedious manual adjustment, so that you can focus on what makes the game fun: expanding your city, reaching your goals and unlocking new content.

Take good care of yourself and until the next one!

notes.title: Gameplay implications of procedurally generated maps
notes.content:
Let’s talk about procedural generation in this latest update.

As mentioned on its Steam Page, [i]Times of Progress[/i] features procedural map generation. But how does it work exactly?

Whenever a new run is started, the map is procedurally generated just from a few high-level variables. These variables will be tweak-able by you in sandbox mode (although not in the beta).

Setting these variables determines how many [i]Water, Rocks, Hill, Mountains, Forest[/i] etc etc tiles that can be found on the generated map. There will be some imbalance, but all resources will be found in some quantity on any map.

This imbalance in turn will determine which industries will be better to develop in the game. Being strong in a certain industry will help with trading with external AI-controlled cities later on to get in exchange those resources and materials that are not readily available or producible locally in your city.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/b846209b307df2c4213ca462368af5ad71de7647.gif][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/b846209b307df2c4213ca462368af5ad71de7647.gif[/img][/url]

Not everything is procedurally generated though. For example each [i]Forest[/i]tile will always yield the same amount of [i]Wood[/i]. Why? Because I don’t want you to spend time min-maxing forever the [i]Wood[/i] yield by checking how much of it each [i]Forest[/i] tile on the map (thousands of them...) will provide. Instead, deciding where to place the [i]Sawmill[/i] should depend on roughly how many [i]Forest[/i] resources are in range of it (which is easy to see), as well as how to connect it to the transportation network and find workers nearby.

Hope these choices will make sense in the upcoming closed beta! If you haven’t signed up already for it, you can do so here: [url=https://subscribepage.io/pressingthumbs]https://subscribepage.io/pressingthumbs[/url].



I have an extra dev update note: I have added some wave effects near the coast and some trails behind ships. This is how they look:

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/01f53f4cf7a5cef90be3771eb6397fae37b543af.gif][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/01f53f4cf7a5cef90be3771eb6397fae37b543af.gif[/img][/url]

They may be a bit faint due to the GIF resolution and compression, but I am hoping they will add to the chill feelings and keep you in the flow during play!

Until the next update! Have a good one in the meantime.

notes.title: Happy citizens means upgraded housing
notes.content:
It’s time for the first update about [i]Times of Progress[/i]! 

In these updates I will dive a bit into the mechanics of the game and explain how the game works. 

Today I will talk about [i]Housing Upgrades[/i]. It’s at least inspired by [i]Caesar III[/i]'s similar mechanic, a game that I completely loved growing up as a kid and sunk hundreds of hours into it.

In [i]Times of Progress[/i] you start by building [i]Towns[/i]. They look like this:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/6d7e52f671c80f14bca7097f79f8eaafe49648e6.png[/img]

There’s no zoning because housing buildings placement is very important and you must be in full control of it. So you decide where individual [i]Towns[/i] go, they will have some basic [i]Needs[/i]. Namely [i]Food[/i], [i]Employment[/i] and [i]Health[/i]. 

Having access to these will keep the citizens happy, but to upgrade to the next level they will also need to have access to a certain degree of [i]Safety[/i] and [i]Basic Education[/i].

Once those are satisfied, they will upgrade to [i]Suburbs[/i]:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/c0de0524a8295d2d1b6acacee88225689a3dca77.png[/img]

[i]Suburbs[/i] host more citizens, which means more workers available and a wider range of influence, so that workers can be employed further away and so on.

To reach the next level and become [i]City[/i] dwellers, they’ll also want access to [i]Higher Education[/i] and [i]Entertainment[/i]. 

[i]Cities[/i] offer yet more space for citizens and have an even wider range. Here is how they look:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44789373/09d639b1822b3def7c37bb2e50cbcd2ef5f5606d.png[/img]

You also need to keep on satisfying those needs, otherwise there’s a risk that citizens become unhappy. If their needs are neglected for too long then their houses will [i]Degrade[/i], which will bring a number of issues that will need to be addressed. But that is a topic for another update.

Until the next one!
